messages.subject: Is scale_y_log2 gone?
parts:
Hi,

I remember that there used to be scale_y_log2. But it seems that it is
not available anymore. Why is it removed?

--
Regards,
Peng

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Re: Is scale_y_log2 gone?
parts: Probably to avoid the large number of scale_y_* functions, to avoid confusion. Much of that functionality was moved to the scales package, and you should be just using the trans argument to scale_y_continuous now, I believe.  See ?scales::log_trans

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Is scale_y_log2 gone?
parts:
Hi:

As Joran mentioned, it was removed to avoid cluttering; scale_log10()
is still in ggplot2, but for other bases you'll need to use the scales
package to define the appropriate log scale function. See the
following pair of references:

Brian Diggs' post re the scales package and defining your own
transformation (most recent posting):
http://blog.ggplot2.org/

The ggplot2-0.9.0 transition guide (see sections 6 and 7):
http://cloud.github.com/downloads/hadley/ggplot2/guide-col.pdf

HTH,
Dennis
